name: pulse-radix-composition
description: Designs Radix-inspired React component composition in this Laravel app. Use when building dialogs, menus, popovers, tabs, accordions, selects, switches, compound components, slots, asChild APIs, portals, or controlled/uncontrolled primitives.
purpose: Avoid reimplementing complex accessibility behaviour and keep component APIs flexible without leaking DOM internals.
single_responsibility: Composition of complex interactive components on Radix primitives: primitive selection, compound parts, slots, asChild, portals, and public data-attribute styling.
triggers: Building a dialog, menu, popover, tabs, accordion, select, or switch
Wrapping or styling Radix UI primitives
Designing compound components with coordinated parts
Using asChild, slots, portals, or state data attributes
completion_criteria: A Radix primitive or native HTML is chosen to fit the interaction's complexity
Radix focus, keyboard, ARIA, disabled, and portal behaviour is preserved
Compound parts and slots are exposed only when consumers need layout control
Styling targets public data attributes, not private DOM structure
Custom `asChild` children spread props and accept/pass refs
validation_criteria: Tests cover public outcomes, not Radix internals
failure_handling: If accessible interaction cannot be preserved with native HTML or an available Radix primitive, stop and report the gap instead of hand-rolling complex keyboard, focus, or ARIA behaviour.
Report any composition, slot, or portal decision left unresolved because the interaction or Radix API is unconfirmed.
escalation_path: Route uncertain Radix primitive or asChild API behaviour through pulse-docs-research (Context7).
Hand semantic, keyboard, and screen-reader requirements to pulse-accessibility-wcag and public prop shape to pulse-api-contract.
Escalate to the user when the required interaction needs a new dependency or a scope change.
responsibilities: Prefer Radix primitives for complex accessible interactions.
Preserve Radix focus, keyboard, ARIA, disabled, and portal behaviour.
Style public data attributes, not private DOM structure.
Ensure custom components used with `asChild` spread props and accept/pass refs so Radix behaviour and accessibility remain intact; use `forwardRef` only when a library contract still requires it.
